profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the backend platform team and the developer productivity/insights team at a mid-sized SaaS company. They are preparing to roll out a lightweight 'team pulse' integration into existing Agile ceremonies across five product squads, based on an internal initiative inspired by research on how happiness and unhappiness affect software engineers in Agile teams. The context is that engineering leadership wants a combined update in two weeks showing both implementation readiness and early cross-team signals. The agenda is to align on the interface between the pulse collection service and the sprint reporting pipeline, confirm what each team will hand off by the end of the week, and clarify how the five pilot squads will be included in the dashboard. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, ownership boundaries, and timing for the pilot handoff and reporting setup.

members.name: Nina Alvarez
members.expertise: Agile delivery practices, internal developer experience tooling, team health instrumentation
members.background: Former scrum master turned engineering manager who now leads internal tools for surveys, retrospectives, and delivery analytics across product engineering.
members.private_state: She needs the pilot to look operational quickly for leadership, wants minimal coordination overhead with other teams, and is trying to avoid reopening any discussion about survey design or organizational change management.
hidden_assumptions: When leadership asks for a 'pilot-ready dashboard,' they mainly need a usable internal view with partial but credible data, not a polished production-grade reporting asset.
The 'five pilot squads' are the five squads that already agreed to try the pulse questions in retrospectives, even if only three have fully wired event export this week.
A team being 'integrated' means its pulse entries can be captured and manually joined to sprint metadata, even if the automated pipeline is not complete.
The shared 'weekly snapshot' should reflect each squad's latest completed sprint because that is the stable Agile reporting unit used by her team.
The backend team will naturally own the durable schema and access controls once her team sends the event shape they have already been testing.

members.name: Raj Patel
members.role: Staff Backend Engineer, Platform Data Services
members.expertise: Event pipelines, analytics schemas, internal APIs, data reliability
members.background: Long-time backend engineer responsible for shared telemetry infrastructure and downstream reporting contracts used by engineering leadership dashboards.
members.private_state: He wants to prevent another loosely defined internal analytics feed from creating maintenance debt, protect his team from ambiguous ownership, and ensure anything called ready can run without manual intervention.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot-ready dashboard' means the underlying feed is stable enough that leadership could rely on it without caveats or hand-edited joins.
The 'five pilot squads' are the five squads listed in the Jira epic for platform onboarding, which means all five should emit through the same automated path before they are counted.
A team being 'integrated' means its events are validated in the platform ingestion service, stored in the canonical schema, and visible in the standard reporting job.
The shared 'weekly snapshot' should be generated on a fixed Monday-Sunday window so all engineering reports align across teams regardless of sprint cadence.
Developer Productivity will continue to own mapping logic and semantic interpretation of pulse responses unless ownership is explicitly transferred.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to have the dashboard 'pilot-ready' for leadership next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means an internal dashboard with enough data from the participating squads to demonstrate trends, even if some joins are manual and some squads are only partially connected.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means an automated, reliable dashboard backed by the canonical pipeline, with no manual patching and all listed pilot squads flowing through the standard reporting path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are used to compressing status for leadership into phrases like 'ready' or 'good for the pilot,' and in coordination meetings people often avoid unpacking quality thresholds unless there is visible disagreement.

misalignment_points.topic: Which squads are 'the five pilot squads'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer several times to 'the five pilot squads' as if this is a single agreed set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the five squads that consented in retro facilitator meetings: Atlas, Beacon, Comet, Delta, and Echo.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the five squads in the platform onboarding Jira epic: Atlas, Beacon, Comet, Foxtrot, and Gemini.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both lists overlap on three well-known squads and the phrase 'the five pilot squads' sounds already established, so neither expects the other to be referencing a different source of truth.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss when each squad will be 'integrated' before the reporting cut.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the survey pulse can be collected and exported in a usable format that her analyst can merge with sprint metadata if needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the squad's events pass schema validation, land in the platform event store, and are consumed by the scheduled reporting job.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-team software coordination, 'integrated' is a normal shorthand that often goes unquestioned because everyone assumes it simply means 'connected enough,' even though the operational bar differs by function.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on including the pulse data in the 'weekly snapshot' sent to engineering leadership.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the snapshot will use each squad's most recent completed sprint as the reporting frame, so squads with different sprint boundaries may contribute data from different calendar weeks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the snapshot is the standard calendar-week export used by all platform dashboards, covering Monday through Sunday only.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both reporting frames are routine internal conventions, and because the phrase 'weekly snapshot' already exists in company reporting language, each assumes the other is using the obvious default.

If we can show a usable internal dashboard with partial but believable data from Atlas, Beacon, Comet, Delta, and Echo, that's enough for next week. I do not want to get dragged into another round of survey design debates or a heavyweight cross-team coordination thread.

If we don't hold that line, my team inherits another messy feed.
